content/DynamicConversations/guides.html.title: Dynamic Conversations Usage Guide | Dynamic Tools Docs
content/DynamicConversations/guides.html.summary: Dynamic Conversations Usage Guide This is a quick start guide for the Dynamic Converations Asset, which goes over the basic functionality and how to start creating your own dialogues. Getting Started After installing the package from the package manager, you can start setting up your interface by creating a Dynamic Text object for the line display, an Image for the portraits, a button prefab for the player choices, an audio source to play line audio, etc. After adding all the necessary components into the Scene and assigning them into the Conversation Runner Controller you can start creating the Scriptable Objects for your conversations. Create Speaker Profile Right click into your project folder, go into the create, Dynamic Tools, Conversations and start by creating a Speaker Profile object. In the speaker profile object, you can set up a configuration for how to display the text such as typing speed, character name, font, dialogue portraits, sound effects and more. Create Sound Effect Asset Creating sound effect assets is also pretty simple, in the same menu select sound effect, and in the inspector add custom audio files and set up the configuration as needed. You can also preview the result by pressing the play preview button. Create a Conversation Then you can create and open the Conversation Tree Editor by double clicking a conversation tree asset. In this window you can start adding lines, choices, wait and event nodes by right clicking and selecting the node, and creating the connections between the nodes is as easy as dragging the output port of a node into the input node of another. Create a Line Node In here you can start writing lines for your own conversation, if you want to have an interesting dynamic look you can start using the rich text implementation to add effects to the text or change certain properties of sections of the line by following this simple syntax: <EffectTag:Value1,Value2...>Your Text</> or <EffectTag:Property1=Value1,Property2=Value2> All the included effects and their tags can be found further down in the Package Contents section. The lines also provide a drop-down menu to select a portrait when it is available from the Current Speaker Profile. Create Player Choices You can use choice nodes to create branching in the conversation. Each choice option results in a different outcome. Create Events Additionally, you could add event nodes to call scene functions during a conversation. This can be done by creating an Event Channel Object of the desired type and then assign it to the respective node. To have a function be called you will canadd the event listener of the correct type into your scene and assign both the channel object and the events to be called. Then when the conversation reaches the specified event node the channel will fire, and the functions set into the event listener will be called. You can also directly subscribe to the event channel fromyour custom scripts! Use the Localization System At the top of the editor window, you can find a language selector. This selector allows you to alternate between different versions of the conversation tree, depending on which language is set during runtime the asset will select the specified version. More information about the Localization system can be found in the package contents section. Use Runtime Text Replacements You can add custom data to be replaced in runtime by using tags encapsulated by brackets like this: [CustomTagName]. You can set the values and their respective tags by using the ConversationReplaceManager functions. For more information check out the Package Contents section. Start Using the Asset! That mostly covers the entire process of creating a dialogue with events and player choices, what's left would be to create your own script to set up the inputs to call the NextLine, FinishLine, ToggleFastForward functions found in the conversation runner script. To further expand on the basic setup, you can subscribe your own functions into the "OnStartConversation" and "OnFinishConversation" events to handle stuff like displaying and hiding the Dialogue UI or enabling and disabling player movement, etc.

content/DynamicEvents/guides.html.title: Dynamic Events Usage Guide | Dynamic Tools Docs
content/DynamicEvents/guides.html.summary: Dynamic Events Usage Guide This is a quick start guide for the Dynamic Events Asset. Event Channels Event channels are scriptable objects that hold event references through a subscription pattern that allow objects to trigger and receive events without requiring a direct reference between them. You can create event channels by using the create asset menu under Dynamic Tools > Events: Each type of event refers to an additional parameter to send when invoking the event, can be used to propagate certain information directly through the event activation. Event Listeners There are two options to listen to event channels: Event Listener Components You can add an event listener component in your scene and assign it an event channel, this allows you to directly select functions to fire using the inspector view for Unity Events. Subscribe from Scripts You can also subscribe to event channels directly into any custom script and run custom code directly from them without using event listener components. Always remember to unsubscribe to the event when the object is disposed to avoid memory leaks or unintended behavior.

content/DynamicSoundFX/guides.html.title: Dynamic SoundFX Usage Guide | Dynamic Tools Docs
content/DynamicSoundFX/guides.html.summary: Dynamic SoundFX Usage Guide This guide covers the basic usage of Sound Effect Assets from the DynamicSoundFX Asset SoundEffect Asset A sound effect asset is a scriptable object that hold configuration for a single instance of a sound effect type that can be reused. It allows setting up various clips, the order on which these clips are played, randomized volume and pitch when playing and the Audio Mixer Group to use when playing the sound. To create a sound effect asset, use the create asset menu into Dynamic Tools > SoundFX

content/DynamicTextFX/guides.html.title: Dynamic TextFX Usage Guide | Dynamic Tools Docs
content/DynamicTextFX/guides.html.summary: Dynamic TextFX Usage Guide This guide covers the basics of using Dynamic Text in your projects, as well as a reference for all existing text effects Dynamic Text Object You can add a Dynamic Text Object using either UI (Canvas) > DynamicTextUGUI or 3D Object > DynamicText from the object menu. You can also add them as components directly into an object in the scene. Dynamic Text UGUI vs Dynamic Text Both objects are functionally the same, each extend from TextMeshProUGUI and TextMeshPro respectively, the only difference is that DynamicTextUGUI is meant to be used in UI Canvas, whie DynamicText can be used in 3D world space. Properties In the inspector, you can edit all the basic text mesh pro properties, with the addition of the Dynamic Text Settings, where you can set up the reveal animation, custom reveal pause config to add an extra wait time after certain characters and custom color presets to create tags that can be used in the color related effects. Text Effects You can add effects to the text using the custom rich-text implementation, you can checkout the reference for all effects lower down this guide. Parsing is updated whenever the text is changed, even in edit mode. The syntax is based on html, and follows this pattern: <effect:property=value,property2=value>Text Content. Alternatively, you can also write it as <effect:value, value2>Text Content</> or even Text Content</> to use the default values. Text Reveal Animations You can select from a variety of reveal animations. These animations cause the text to set characters as visible one by one, using the specified animation, speed and mode. The mode defines when the text reveal is played. It can happen whenever the text is changed, only on awake, only on enable or never play automatically. You can manually trigger a reveal animation to play calling the RevealText() function in DynamicText objects Text Effect References Name Tag Effect Wobble <wobble:Speed, Strength> Shake <shake:Speed, Strength> Collapse <collapse:Strength, Delay> Color <color:ColorTag> or <color:r,g,b,a> Rainbow <rainbow:Speed> Rainbow wave <rainbowwave:Speed> Scale <scale:Strength> Breathing <breathing:Speed, Strength> Fall <fall:Strength, Start, Delay> Gradient <gradient:Speed, Color1, Color2, ...> Gradient wave <gradientwave:Speed, Color1, Color2, ...>

index.html.summary: Dynamic Tools Docs Welcome to the official documentation for the Dynamic Tools suite of Unity Assets! You can get the Tools from my page on the Unity Asset store! If you're enjoying the tools feel free to leave a review or rating to the assets, it helps out a ton! The assets are sold separately, but you get any dependencies for free! (Ex: Buying Dynamic Conversations gives free access to Dynamic SoundFX, Dynamic TextFX and Dynamic Events) Guides Here you can access some usage guides for specific assets! Dynamic Conversations Dynamic TextFX Dynamic SoundFX Dynamic Events API Reference Here you can access the full documentation for all classes, methods and properties from the C# code. The reference includes the documentation for the entire suite of tools, inside you can check information about classes, namespaces, methods and properties for every single asset in the suite. View Reference Index About the assets These assets were created by SoyVixterDev (that's me!) They started as tools to be used in my own projects, but evolved into something larger, and I took it as a chance to provide it as a tool and side project as a Unity Asset for the Asset Store. Originally, the entire project was under the Dynamic Conversations umbrella, but I eventually decided to compartmentalize it into different tools, so every project can import which ever match their needs. The main appeal of the suite is still the Dialogue system, but it now counts with some useful systems and utilities to quickly improve workflows or game polish.
